problem: Existing navigation world models (e.g. NWM) produce visually plausible frames but lack action-conditioned consistency, so multi-step rollouts drift from the true trajectory and mislead MPC planning. Existing few-step diffusion distillation matches distributions rather than rollout consistency, and NWM degrades badly at 5 DDIM steps.
motivation: MPC planning scores imagined rollouts, so drift between imagined and real outcomes leads to failures on the real robot. Real-time deployment also needs few-step inference. Teacher-forced training conditions on ground truth while deployment conditions on the model's own predictions, so error compounds.
key_idea: Post-train a pretrained CDiT navigation world model with self-forcing rollouts and an observation-level LPIPS consistency loss, updating only AdaLN LoRA, and use an inference-consistent state as rollout context so that few-step DDIM sampling stays consistent.
insight: Perceptual (LPIPS) supervision on self-rolled frames is what makes the post-training work: L1/L2 losses collapse (FID 16s of 341-352 vs 93.12). Structure pretraining is needed first (ACC-only on MMK2-RealNav gives FID 196.72 vs 98.17 for two-stage). Using the inference-consistent state as context beats using raw truncated estimates (FID 109.75 -> 93.12), and the 5-step MWM beats 25-step NWM.
method: Stage I structure pretraining: teacher-forced action-conditioned diffusion (CDiT-XL, 1B, 4-frame context) with x0-prediction MSE loss; action and timestep injected via AdaLN, and past states attended via cross-attention.

Stage II ACC post-training: self-forcing-style autoregressive rollout of N=8 steps, random truncation denoising step with stop-gradient on intermediate steps, and gradient only through the final prediction conditioned on self-generated context.
ACC loss: multi-frame averaged LPIPS between rollout predictions and ground-truth frames; CDiT backbone frozen and only LoRA (r=64, alpha=16) on AdaLN modulation layers trained for 1.5K steps.

ICSD: because timestep and action share AdaLN, post-training also adapts timestep conditioning for few-step sampling; a deterministic DDIM update builds an inference-consistent state s^IC, used as autoregressive context instead of the blurry truncated estimate.
Planning: NWM-style MPC with CEM over action sequences in rollout space, scoring the terminal frame by negative LPIPS to the goal image; DDIM 5 steps for MWM.

setting.backbone: CDiT-XL world model (1B params, initialized from NWM), trained with LoRA on AdaLN in post-training
setting.training_data: SCAND (8.7h, 138 trajectories; Stage I skipped since NWM init already trained on it) and self-collected MMK2-RealNav (18 trajectories, 2h, 1.3km)
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB (4-frame context) plus goal image
setting.action_space: planar action sequences (CEM-sampled) executed open-loop on the base
setting.simulator: none (offline datasets SCAND / MMK2-RealNav; real world)

numbers.extra: CEM 1 iteration, 120 samples, each simulated 3 times with best outcome
numbers.evidence: Tab. Goal-image navigation performance on SCAND with CEM planning: MWM (ours) 1.14 / 0.302

numbers.eval_set_note: real robot, four goal locations (cabinet, window, pillar, corridor), open-loop one-shot planning
numbers.extra: CEM 3 iterations x 120 samples, open-loop, RGB only, remote GPU inference
numbers.evidence: Tab. Quantitative real-world goal-image navigation results aggregated over four targets: MWM 0.30 / 2.16

numbers_note: No standard VLN/ObjNav benchmarks. World-model quality results (LPIPS/DreamSim/FID at 1-16s, rollout time 2.3s vs 9.6s for NWM DDIM25) are in the tables but not listed here. SR in the real-world table is printed as a fraction (0.30).
results: On SCAND, MWM gets ATE 1.14 and RPE 0.302 versus NWM's 1.28 and 0.33. With 5-step DDIM it beats NWM at 25 steps on LPIPS, DreamSim and FID (16s DreamSim 0.337 vs 0.373) with a rollout time of 2.3s versus 9.6s. In the real world, SR is 0.30 and NE 2.16 versus NWM's 0.20 and 3.18 and NoMaD's 0.08 and 2.88.
limitations: Planning is open-loop and one-shot with no online replanning.
Real-world evaluation is small (four goals, one indoor floor, one robot), with low absolute success (0.30).
Only the terminal-frame LPIPS goal objective is used, and Stage I was skipped on SCAND because of the pretrained initialization.
